title.before: Whole-abdominal radiation followed by COP/doxorubicin for feline high-grade lymphoma
title.after: Whole-abdomen radiation followed by COP/doxorubicin for feline high-grade gastrointestinal lymphoma

intervention.before: Whole-abdominal radiation induction followed by COP/doxorubicin chemotherapy
intervention.after: Whole-abdomen radiation therapy followed by COP/doxorubicin chemotherapy

contact.before: University of Missouri Veterinary Health Center Oncology / Oncology Clinical Trials service

notes.before: Strong current pipeline lead, but a research award is not the same as an owner-facing recruiting protocol. Keep on watchlist and out of matching until Missouri publishes recruitment/eligibility or confirms enrollment.
notes.after: The current official named protocol now explicitly invites enrollment, replacing the earlier award-only watch signal. High-grade/large-cell GI disease and absence of lymphoma outside the abdomen require investigator confirmation; a general lymphoma match is prescreening only. Radiation is delivered during the first week, followed by COP/doxorubicin. Screening, chemotherapy, other care and travel coverage are not stated. This is distinct from the Texas A&M small-cell GI lymphoma radiation protocol.

special_requirement.after: Cytology or histopathology must confirm high-grade / large-cell gastrointestinal lymphoma confined to the abdomen. No previous chemotherapy; FeLV/FIV-negative and suitable for anesthesia. Investigator screening includes blood count, chemistry, urinalysis, chest radiographs and abdominal ultrasound. Visits in Columbia, Missouri weekly for at least eight weeks, then every three weeks for five more visits.

status.before: Newly funded FY2027 study — patient enrollment not yet independently confirmed
status.after: Currently enrolling — University of Missouri Veterinary Health Center

funding.before: EveryCat Health Foundation award: $50,000; owner-level covered costs have not yet been published.
funding.after: Partially funded. The study covers whole-abdomen radiation and provides a $1,000 credit for care at the VHC after radiation is completed. Published information does not specify screening, COP/doxorubicin chemotherapy, other care or travel coverage; confirm these costs with the study team.

funding_status.after: Partially funded; radiation covered and $1,000 VHC credit after radiation
